preamble: Spirantization of the uvular ejective: [qʼ] loses its glottal closure and becomes the voiced uvular fricative [ʁ]. In Udi, the Lezgic language of Nij and Oghuz in Azerbaijan, several words reconstructed with Proto-Lezgian *q̇ (StarLing's notation for qʼ; capital I marks pharyngealization) show ʁ, while Lezgian, Tabasaran, Agul and Rutul keep the ejective: *jiq̇Iʷ 'back, middle' > Udi biʁI (Lezgian juq̇), *q̇IoʁIo-r 'hedgehog' > Udi ʁIaʁIal (Lezgian q̇üʁür). Archi iʁI-da 'in the middle' shows the same outcome. The change is not regular: Udi also loses *q̇ entirely in some words (*q̇äl 'salt' > el), keeps an ejective in others (moʁI ~ moq:I 'soot', where Udi q: is StarLing's notation for the Udi ejective), and the conditioning between ʁ and loss is unclear. The comparisons rest on Starostin's Proto-Lezgian reconstruction (Nikolayev & Starostin 1994), which is not universally accepted.

examples.note: Lezgian juq̇, Tabasaran juq̇I, Kryz jiq̇. Nikolayev and Starostin derive the Udi form via *wiq̇I.
Lezgian q̇üʁür, Tabasaran q̇IuʁIur, Kryz q̇üʁer.
Agul riq̇, Rutul rɨq̇, Archi diq̇.
Archi iq̇Iʷ, Rutul juq̇I-dɨ. The variant with h shows the outcome was not stable.

sources: Nikolayev, S. L. & Starostin, S. A. (1994). A North Caucasian Etymological Dictionary. Moscow: Asterisk. Lezghian database online at StarLing: https://starlingdb.org/cgi-bin/response.cgi?root=config&basename=%2fdata%2fcauc%2flezget
